title: Close an inside-fitting pressure cooker
keywords: oval lid through a smaller mouth
instruction: Close the pressure cooker, ready to go on the stove.
context: Inside-fitting (inner-lid) pressure cookers are an everyday pot in millions of homes. The lid is larger than the oval mouth: it goes in only tilted and crosswise, has to be turned in line inside, and falls back into the cooker unless it is pulled up against the rim and the locking loop is put over the handles.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. The table top is the kitchen counter. (1) A 1.5 litre inside-fitting pressure cooker body (Hawkins Classic type, 3.25 mm aluminium), loose on the counter, its axis 34 cm forward and 16 cm right of the centre line: a 130 mm flat base, a 159 mm body, its rim's top 105 mm above the counter, with a 3 mm lip running in to an oval mouth 120 x 138 mm (the long axis across the handle). Body 1.04 kg plus 0.40 kg of rice and water, 22 mm deep. A black bakelite body handle (130 x 26 x 28 mm, top 102.5 mm above the counter) on a steel bracket points left and toward the robot at 45 degrees; on the bracket, 93 mm from the cooker's axis, a 6 x 10.5 mm steel pivot post with its top 116.5 mm above the counter; under the handle's end, a hook pocket for the locking loop. (2) The lid, 0.21 kg, lying top up on the counter, its middle 42 cm forward and 38 cm right, its handle pointing toward the robot at right angles to the body handle: an oval aluminium plate 128 x 146 x 2.5 mm (4 mm larger than the mouth all round) edged with a 5 mm black rubber gasket, a vent tube in the middle, a 10 x 8 mm steel handle bar running 150 mm out from the vent tube to a 110 x 22 x 20 mm black bakelite lid handle (its end 25 mm past the body handle's when closed), and, hinged at the lid handle's end, a steel locking loop (3.5 mm wire, 44 mm wide, 60 mm long, 8 g) lying folded out on the counter. Seated, the lid's gasket presses up against the underside of the rim's lip, the handle bar lies on the pivot, and the lid handle sits 2 mm above the body handle; with nothing holding it the lid swings down into the cooker about the pivot. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Judged at the end, except the failures, which count at any time. Seated: eight points round the top of the lid's gasket, at its outer edge, are each in under the rim (at least 1 mm outside the mouth's edge) and within 1.5 mm of the rim's underside, the lid is level with the cooker within 3 degrees, and it is in contact with the cooker (measured: the gasket overlaps and touches the rim all round, a 1.5 mm feeler gauge passes nowhere; photo). Latched: the locking loop is swung in 34-50 degrees from hanging, its crossbar touches the cooker in the pocket under the body handle's end, and the lid handle's underside is within 4 mm of the body handle's top at the handles' end (measured: by eye the loop is over the handles' end, and the lid handle cannot be lifted off the body handle by hand). Hands off: no finger pad touches the lid, the loop or the cooker, and each gripper is at least 5 cm from the lid handle's end and from the loop. 1.0: seated, latched and hands off; 0.5: seated; 0.25: the lid was at some time wholly inside the cooker, below the rim (measured: from the video); else 0.0. 0.0 for good if at any time the cooker tips more than 25 degrees, or the cooker or the lid falls off the counter. A lid that is not latched swings back down into the cooker as soon as it is let go, so it cannot stay seated with the hands off. The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held for 1 s with the cooker, the lid and the loop still.
reset_notes: Open the cooker (squeeze the handles, swing the loop out, take the lid out the way it went in) and lay the lid top up on the counter at its marks, its handle toward the robot.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim, PhysX, 20 Hz control). Real size and mass; the lid and mouth sizes are estimates (maker gives a 12 cm mouth class). The gasket is rigid (a real one compresses 1-2 mm when the handles are squeezed), so the loop's catch is a pocket shaped as an arc round its hinge that latches without that travel. The handle bar is rigid on the lid (real: some play). Rice and water are a rigid 0.40 kg layer. Cameras 1280 x 704 (Dream-1 sees 320 x 176).
